guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our model’s case for Memphis starts with offensive flexibility. We rate the Memphis passing game well above Army’s pass defense, and the rushing matchup also favors the home offense. That matters because Memphis does not appear dependent on one specific path to create separation; our numbers suggest it can challenge Army through either phase.

The counterweight is Army’s rushing offense against a Memphis run defense that has graded poorly. Cale Hellums rushed for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns last season, while Godspower Nwawuihe carried 20 times for 98 yards against South Florida. Army also averaged more than 34 minutes of possession through its first two games. We see a credible path for Army to sustain drives and reduce the number of possessions, which is especially relevant when evaluating a favorite.

For us, the disagreement with the market comes from Memphis having multiple favorable offensive matchups. The reason we still pass is that Army’s ability to control the game on the ground creates enough resistance that the available price does not offer sufficient value.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Army’s rushing offense against the Memphis front. Army produced 25 runs of at least 10 yards through three weeks, while our efficiency numbers identify run defense as Memphis’ clearest vulnerability. If Memphis limits those gains and forces Army out of favorable down-and-distance situations, the game can open up for the more balanced home offense. If not, Army can compress the game and make separation more difficult.

recent_game.fact: Army lost 28-24 to South Florida on Sept. 12, leaving the Black Knights 1-1 overall and 0-1 in the American Conference.
Against South Florida, quarterback Cale Hellums completed 9 of 10 passes for 91 yards and two touchdowns; his .900 completion percentage was a career high.
Godspower Nwawuihe led Army against South Florida with 20 carries for 98 yards and scored a 10-yard fourth-quarter rushing touchdown.
Zach Mundell caught three passes against South Florida, including a 24-yard touchdown from Cale Hellums, and completed a 37-yard pass to Godspower Nwawuihe.

opponent_notes.fact: Army's 2026 schedule lists a road game at Memphis on Oct. 31 with kickoff time to be determined.

quarterback.fact: Senior Cale Hellums is Army's first-team quarterback, followed on the depth chart by sophomore Bryson Luter and sophomore Ethan Washington.
Hellums returned as Army's starting quarterback after making 10 starts and appearing in every game in 2025.
Hellums rushed for 1,223 yards and 18 touchdowns in 2025; the 18 rushing touchdowns were the second-most in an Army season.
Through two games in 2026, Hellums had 142 rushing yards, 150 passing yards and a team-high four total touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Godspower Nwawuihe is listed as Army's first-team running back ahead of Jake Rendina and Carson Smith.
Army identified Nwawuihe as its feature back for 2026 after his breakout performance in the 2025 Fenway Bowl.
Senior Samari Howard is the first-team slotback, with Zach Mundell and David Clerk also listed at the position.
Mundell returned in 2026 after playing only one game from 2024 through 2025; he rushed for 105 yards and two touchdowns on four carries against Bryant.
Army's listed first-team offensive line is left tackle Henry Appleton, left guard Kyle Kloska, center Brady Small, right guard Paolo Gennarelli and right tackle Teddy Williams.
The second-team offensive linemen are left tackle Xavier Archawski, left guard Ben Britton, center Chuck Johnson, right guard Sam Waters and right tackle Brandon Wraalstad.
Army's first-team receiving personnel consists of wide receiver Brady Anderson, wide receiver Tobi Olawole, wide receiver Kavon Pointer and tight end Parker Poloskey.

defensive_personnel.fact: Army's listed starting defensive front is Dillon Stowers at defensive tackle, Kody Harris-Miller at nose tackle and Jack Bousum at defensive end.
The listed starting linebackers are Noah Nixon at outside linebacker, Jaquavious Moss and Elijah Walton at inside linebacker, and Zane Tallman at nickelback.
Army's listed starting secondary is cornerbacks Jaydan Mayes and Jaxon Hammond, strong safety Caleb Williams and free safety Stephen Nnadozie.
Through two games, Elijah Walton and Jaquavious Moss shared the team lead with 12 tackles each; Dillon Stowers led Army with one sack.

coaching_changes.fact: John Holt is in his first season as co-offensive line coach alongside third-year co-offensive line coach Cheston Blackshear.
Jamere Hogue is in his first season as defensive line coach, and Munir Prince is in his first season as cornerbacks coach.
Cody Worley is Army's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, while Daryl Dixon is defensive coordinator and Scot Sloan is co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.

offensive_context.fact: Through two games, Army averaged 394.0 rushing yards, 497.5 total yards and 41.5 points per game.
Army led the American Conference in rushing offense at 394.0 yards per game and ranked second in the conference in total offense at 497.5 yards per game.
Army had not thrown an interception through its first two games and had allowed one sack.
Army averaged 34:22 of possession through two games.
Zach Mundell, Godspower Nwawuihe and Cale Hellums each had at least 140 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns through two games.
Army had 25 rushing plays of at least 10 yards through three weeks, tied for sixth nationally.

defensive_context.fact: Through two games, Army allowed 15.5 points and 267.0 total yards per game, including 98.5 rushing yards and 168.5 passing yards per game.
Army's 267.0 yards allowed per game ranked first in the American Conference and 25th nationally through three weeks.

special_teams.fact: Senior James Wagenseller is Army's first-team punter, junior Dawson Jones is the first-team kicker and senior Owen Walter is the first-team long snapper.
Samari Howard and Jaydan Mayes are listed as co-first-team kickoff returners, while Lloyd Benson III is the first-team punt returner.
Army averaged 47.6 yards per punt through two games, and Wagenseller was selected to the Ray Guy Award's Ray's 8 for Week 2.
Lloyd Benson III averaged 18.7 yards per punt return through two games.
